FAQ.title: Questions people actually ask
FAQ.description: If something is still unclear, email us — a human replies.

items.question: Does VidSmaller add a watermark?
items.answer: No. Not on the free tier, not anywhere. Your compressed file is identical to the original apart from the encoding.

items.question: How much smaller will my video get?
items.answer: It depends on the source. Phone and screen recordings are usually badly encoded and routinely drop 70–90%. Footage that is already tightly compressed may only shrink 20–40%. The Balanced preset targets roughly half the original size.

items.question: Do I need to create an account?
items.answer: Not to try it. Signed-out visitors get a couple of free compressions per day with a 200 MB file limit. Signing in raises that to 1 GB and unlocks the batch queue.

items.question: What happens to my files?
items.answer: Your browser uploads it straight to our own storage bucket over a one-time link, the encoder pulls it from there, and that staged copy is deleted the moment the job finishes. The compressed result expires after two hours for anonymous jobs, up to seven days when you are signed in. We never watch, train on, share or resell your footage.

items.question: Which formats can I upload?
items.answer: MP4, MOV, MKV, AVI, WebM, FLV, WMV, M4V, MPEG, 3GP, TS, MTS, VOB and more — 20+ containers in total. You can also change the output container to MP4, MKV, WebM or MOV.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: Most clips under five minutes finish in under a minute. Longer files and slower encoder settings take proportionally more time; you can close the tab and come back.

items.question: What is a credit?
items.answer: A credit is one billed encoder minute — we charge exactly what the encoder charges us. Every job runs import, compress and export, and each stage is billed a full minute, so the floor is 3 credits. That 3 covers any 1080p clip up to about seven minutes, because the encode itself only crosses into a second minute past that point; a 15-minute meeting recording is 4 credits, a 40-minute 4K file is 7. H.265 costs more because it is roughly 3.8x slower to encode. Failed jobs are refunded in full, once.

items.question: Can I compress a 4K or 1 GB file?
items.answer: Yes. Free accounts cap out at 1 GB per file, Pro at 1.4 GB. 4K works on every plan — it just costs more credits, because bigger frames take longer to encode.
